equivalents.note: The Tibetan translates the rāga name as 'giving what is desired', as if it were Sanskrit kāmada, 'granting wishes'.
The Tibetan reads beṇī as rdzing, 'pool', not 'braid' (dbus su rdzing bcas, 'with a pool in the middle'), and keeps dbus su rdzing in the comment (cp.13.m3).
The Tibetan has mnyen pa, apparently 'boatman' (compare mnyan pa), the word it also uses for kaṇṇahāra, 'helmsman', in cp.13.5a, so the five tathāgatas are made boatmen rather than oars.
The Tibetan makes Kāṇha's body (kAh+Na lus) the one that ferries across (sgrol byed) out of illusion, one construal of the unclear bāhaa kāa kāhnila.
The same word, mnyen pa, stands for keṛuāla, 'oar', in cp.13.3a, so it is not a distinctive equivalent of kaṇṇahāra.

The Tibetan takes māṅge as the boat itself (stong nyid grur 'jug, 'enters the boat of emptiness'), as in song 8 it took the word as the boat's stern and prow, where Munidatta has mārga, 'path' (cp.13.m6).
The Tibetan turns sāṅge, 'with', into a noun, making Kāṇha 'the companion of great bliss' (bde ba chen po'i grogs), and has zhon nas, 'having embarked', for calila, 'went'.
The Tibetan has glu gzhan gyis, 'with another song', for taiś caryā[padair], 'with those caryā verses', rendering the caryā verse simply as 'song'.
Here citta, in kāyavākcitta, is yid rather than sems, and the Tibetan then makes 'that mind' (yid de) the one that dissolves in the fourth refuge, where the Sanskrit has the three dissolve.
The Tibetan renders siddhiḥ, 'accomplishment', with the verb bsgrub, 'accomplish', rather than the noun dngos grub.
Here the Tibetan renders the title as mdo, 'sūtra', where in cp.13.m4 it transcribes it (sU ta ke).

For cittakarṇadhāraṃ the Tibetan has sems gdos pa 'dzin par, 'the mind as holder of the gdos pa', where 'dzin pa answers to dhāra but gdos pa is unclear here, not the mnyen pa of the verse (cp.13.5a).

questions: keruala (kelipātaṃ) in cp.13.m4: not matched. In its place the Tibetan reads rang gi lus mnyam par yongs su shes par bya'o, 'one should fully know one's own body as equal (mnyam par)'; mnyam par stands where kelipātaṃ does but does not mean 'oar', and may be a slip for mnyen par (compare mnyen pa in cp.13.3a), so I have not entered it.

mahasukha-cakra (mahāsukhacakradvīpaṃ) in cp.13.m6: not matched. The Tibetan has bde ba chen po'i gling dang mtshungs par 'gro bar byed do, 'goes as to (literally 'like') the island of great bliss', with no word for cakra ('khor lo), so the term itself is not rendered here.

body in cp.13.m2 (nijadehe → rang lus) and cp.13.m4 (svadehaṃ → rang gi lus), and sukha in cp.13.m3 (sukhaṃ → bde ba), use the same words as the entries given for cp.13.1b, cp.13.3b and cp.13.m2, so they are not entered again.
